title: Hypothesis Testing & p-values
interviewAnswer: A p-value is the probability, assuming the null hypothesis and test assumptions are true, of seeing a result at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
why: Data Scientist interviews often test whether you can reason about experiments instead of mechanically running scipy.stats functions.
intuition: Start by assuming there is no real effect (the null). Ask how surprising your observed result would be under that assumption. A small p-value means the observation would be unusual under the null—it does not directly tell you the probability that the null is false.
deepDive: A hypothesis test requires a null/alternative, a test statistic, assumptions and a decision threshold. Type I error is a false positive; Type II is a false negative. Statistical significance is not necessarily business significance, which is why effect size and confidence intervals matter.
math: p-value = P(test statistic at least as extreme as observed | H₀ and assumptions)
code:
from scipy import stats
# Example: compare two independent sample means
a = [10, 11, 9, 12, 10]
b = [13, 14, 12, 13, 15]
stat, p = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
print(stat, p)
commonMistakes: “p=0.03 means there is a 97% chance the alternative is true.” — incorrect.
Choosing the test after repeatedly looking at results.
followUps: Type I vs Type II error?
When would you use a non-parametric test?
How does multiple testing change interpretation?
production: In product experimentation, predefine the primary metric, sample-size/power plan, stopping rule and guardrail metrics before observing the result.
workedExample: A tiny conversion lift can be statistically significant with millions of users but economically irrelevant. Always report effect size and uncertainty.

lab.goal: Compute a simple two-sample mean test and connect the statistic to the null hypothesis.
lab.buildIt:
import math
a=[10,11,9,12,10,11]; b=[13,12,14,11,13,14]
def mean(x): return sum(x)/len(x)
def var(x):
    m=mean(x); return sum((v-m)**2 for v in x)/(len(x)-1)
se=math.sqrt(var(a)/len(a)+var(b)/len(b))
t=(mean(b)-mean(a))/se
print('difference',mean(b)-mean(a),'t statistic',t)
